memory_candidates.content: When wiring a new gating step into a shared CI workflow file that multiple concurrent tasks also edit, place the new step(s) directly before the terminal always-run reporting step rather than at a fixed position relative to another named step. Re-read the file immediately before each edit (not just once at the start): if sibling tasks commit their own additions to the same insertion point mid-session, the convention of always appending right before the terminal step keeps every insertion order-independent and merge-safe, since git diff against HEAD only shows your own hunk once the siblings have committed theirs.

To locally approximate a GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest runner's minimal PATH on a NixOS development machine, do not use the literal /usr/bin:/bin template (NixOS does not populate those paths with bash/git/find/etc.) -- instead build PATH from `dirname "$(command -v <tool>)"` for each required tool. This preserves the intent (a minimal, explicit tool set) without assuming an FHS directory layout.

The write-time validate-no-task-references.sh hook blocks Write/Edit calls that introduce task-number citations even in throwaway/scratch content (e.g. a temporary CI-violation test comment naming the current task number). When a test needs to deliberately trip a task-reference-style check (C9 in check-module-invariants.sh), use a different gated check that produces the same class of failure without naming a task number (e.g. C10's stale FormalSystem/{docs,latex,typst} path check) rather than fighting the hook.
